strategy.evidence_chain: Profile evidence: 4_1's warp-sliced GEMM1 dequant is the largest successful speedup so far, moving the candidate to 544.480 us and the promoted source to 424.832 us. Code evidence: the current stage1_activation_warp_k_kernel maps one warp to one (tk,i) output and every adjacent i reloads the same hidden_states[t, :] vector from global memory. Prior evidence: the old shared-hidden GEMM1 attempt regressed because it kept scalar per-output K loops, but the current warp-sliced version creates a new reuse surface: adjacent warps in the same CTA process the same tk and can share hidden K blocks while still using vectorized packed FP4 loads. Reference evidence: local NVFP4 GEMV guidance emphasizes wide loads, cache-policy separation, reuse of the vector operand, and register budgeting for memory-bound low-batch FP4 work. Inference: after K-parallelization, hidden-row reloads across I columns are a remaining dequant-side waste. Action: add a tiled GEMM1 fast path that reuses hidden K blocks across adjacent intermediate outputs.
strategy.expected_impact: Should lower hidden memory traffic and improve L1/shared reuse in the dominant GEMM1 path without touching routing or GEMM2 behavior.
strategy.risks: Shared memory staging and extra synchronizations can erase the gain, and accumulator/register pressure can reduce occupancy. Keep the old warp-per-output path as fallback for non-qwen shapes or if the tile assumptions fail.
